headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: nullclaw can read/write broad workspace and network data while godot_rl_agents is a non-runnable game-playing repo with no shared-channel protections.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no I/O surfaces or runnable execution path, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs. B can read/write files, use MCP, browsers, and stdin/stdout, so if operators manually bridge content into A’s repo or prompts, injection is possible but requires unusual setup. The pair lacks a documented shared channel.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B-generated text into A-facing prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or MCP bridge is added between the agents, B can feed attacker-controlled content into A.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any manual copy-paste bridge between B outputs and A inputs.
Restrict B’s MCP targets to trusted, provenance-tagged sources.
Add a review step before any B output is reused in A-related prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches workspace files, audit logs, memory, and secrets, and has broad network egress; A is a docs-only repo with no data classes touched. There is no direct evidence A receives sensitive data, but B’s default surfaces can leak whatever it processes if operators place secrets in its workspace. The interaction is inferred, so uncertainty stays above low.
conditions: IF secrets or customer data are placed in B’s workspace or memory namespace, B can expose them over network egress.
IF A is used as a source repository for sensitive artifacts, those artifacts may be copied into B’s writable workspace.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in B’s workspace.
Rotate or redact any tokens before B processes files.
Use separate OS users for A and B.
Disable B network egress when handling sensitive material.
Store A and B artifacts in separate directories.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capabilities, while B can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses. That makes overlapping mutable-resource access plausible only if both are pointed at the same repo or workspace; the profiles do not prove that, so the conflict is real but not default-dangerous. Uncertainty prevents a lower rating.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to operate on the same git checkout, B can overwrite A-managed files.
IF A is given write access through an external wrapper, concurrent edits can race with B.
mitigations: Assign distinct directories to each agent.
Lock the git checkout before B writes.
Run B in read-only mode for A-owned artifacts.
Use separate branches for any shared repository work.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can act on files, webhooks, and APIs, so if A’s outputs are fed into B without verification, B may operationalize incorrect content. A is a game-playing repo with no documented output-validation contract, so the pairwise pathway is inferred rather than directly evidenced. That supports medium rather than low because B has downstream action authority.
conditions: IF A-generated text is passed into B as authoritative input, B may execute or publish it without verification.
IF B is configured to send webhooks or commit git changes based on A output, errors can cascade downstream.
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A output.
Add schema validation for any A-to-B handoff.
Log and diff A outputs before B consumes them.
Disable B action-taking for unverified inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles secrets, audit logs, workspace files, and conversation history, while A is an open-source repo with no touched data classes. The main compliance risk is retention or residency mismatch if regulated data is processed by B’s logged, networked surfaces; A is not the primary compliance driver here. No direct evidence of a specific regime mismatch exists, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is processed through B’s conversation history or audit logs, retention obligations may be violated.
IF A artifacts contain jurisdiction-bound data and are copied into B’s workspace, residency controls may be bypassed.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in B logs.
Set short retention on B audit logs.
Redact personal data before ingestion.
Keep jurisdiction-bound data out of B’s workspace.
Review B’s data handling policy before deployment.
